title: Economizer
model_title: Boiler Economizer (Serpentine Tube Bank in the Flue-Gas Duct)

introduction.definition: An economizer is a heat exchanger in the boiler flue-gas path that preheats the feedwater before it enters the drum, using heat that would otherwise go up the stack. Banks of serpentine (often finned) tubes carry the water upward while the gas flows down across them — counter-flow.
key_points: Recovers flue-gas heat → higher boiler efficiency
Rule of thumb: ~ 1 % fuel saving per ~ 20–25 °C stack-temperature reduction
Gas must stay above acid dew point
Water must not steam in a non-steaming economizer
introduction.summary: An economizer recovers heat from boiler flue gas to preheat the feedwater before it enters the drum. Banks of (often finned) serpentine tubes sit in the gas duct after the main heating surfaces. Gas flows down while water flows up — counter-flow — so the gas leaves cooler and boiler efficiency rises.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Recovered heat Q = m_gas · cp · (T_gas,in − T_gas,out) = m_w · cp · (T_w,out − T_w,in).

temperature.title: Gas cools as it gives heat to the water
temperature.description: Flue gas enters at the top hot (orange) and leaves the bottom cooler (blue-green), while feedwater flows upward — counter-flow. Gas outlet temperature must stay above the acid dew point when the fuel contains sulphur, to avoid cold-end corrosion; water must stay below saturation to avoid steaming in the economizer.

video_tutorials.title: Economizer — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Economizer.
An economizer is a heat exchanger in the boiler flue-gas path that preheats the feedwater before it enters the drum, using heat that would otherwise go up the stack.
Banks of serpentine (often finned) tubes carry the water upward while the gas flows down across them — counter-flow.
Typical applications include water-tube and packaged boilers; HRSGs (economizer section); shell boilers (add-on stack economizers).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Gas Duct Casing (gas flows downward).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Economizer — Operation

script.narration: How the Economizer works.
Flue gas enters the top of the duct and flows downward.
Feedwater enters the bottom header.
Water rises through the serpentine tubes, absorbing heat.
The soot blower cleans deposits from the fins.
Ash falls to the hopper; heated water goes to the drum.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Flue gas enters at the top hot (orange) and leaves the bottom cooler (blue-green), while feedwater flows upward — counter-flow.

video_tutorials.title: Economizer — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Economizer.
Monitor gas and water temperatures and ΔP.
Operate soot blowers; inspect for erosion.
Thickness survey of tubes; replace eroded/corroded sections.
Watch for cold-end (acid) corrosion: tube leaks at the gas outlet end. Common cause: gas below acid dew point (sulphur fuels), low feedwater temperature.
Watch for fouling/erosion: rising ΔP; thinning. Common cause: ash deposits, high gas velocity.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
